summary: This note is an overview of the Cleveland Indians, an American professional baseball team based in Cleveland, Ohio, that plays in the American League Central division of Major League Baseball. It covers the team's home ballpark, spring training site, and championship history since becoming a major league franchise in 1901. It notes that the team's current World Series drought is the longest active one among MLB's 30 teams.
one_line: Overview of the Cleveland Indians, a Cleveland, Ohio MLB team in the American League Central, with its ballparks and championship history.
key_facts: The Cleveland Indians are an American professional baseball team based in Cleveland, Ohio.
The Cleveland Indians compete in Major League Baseball as a member club of the American League Central division.
The Cleveland Indians have played at Progressive Field since a date given as a blank in the note.
The Cleveland Indians' spring training facility is Goodyear Ballpark in Goodyear, Arizona.
The Cleveland Indians were established as a major league franchise in 1901.
The Cleveland Indians have won two World Series championships, in 1920 and 1948.
The Cleveland Indians have won 10 Central Division titles and six American League pennants.
The Cleveland Indians' current World Series championship drought is the longest active drought among all 30 current Major League teams.
